description: Render actual vs. expected architecture as a mermaid/DOT graph with conflict overlay, drill-down, and per-domain filtering; keyboard-navigable with accessible text alternatives required.

requirements.description: The UI must render actual vs. expected architecture as a mermaid or DOT graph (AC-UI-GRAPH-RENDER) with a conflict overlay highlighting nodes and edges involved in detected conflicts (AC-UI-GRAPH-CONFLICTS). Per-domain filtering must allow users to isolate and inspect individual domains (AC-UI-GRAPH-FILTER). The graph view must be keyboard-navigable and provide accessible text alternatives for all visual elements (AC-UI-GRAPH-A11Y). The UI must consume only generated Connect clients per AC-UI-PROTO-PARITY.
requirements.title: UI Graph Visualization with Conflict Overlay and Accessibility

validation.notes: AC-UI-GRAPH-RENDER: Graph component renders a valid mermaid or DOT string from a fixture graph snapshot without errors
AC-UI-GRAPH-CONFLICTS: Conflict overlay applies a visually distinct style (color/border) to nodes referenced in conflict locations
AC-UI-GRAPH-FILTER: Selecting a domain hides all nodes and edges not belonging to that domain
AC-UI-GRAPH-A11Y: Every graph node has an aria-label or text alternative describing its path and domain
BAS: UI graph view loads with fixture scenario data and displays both actual and expected graph layers
BAS: Clicking a conflicted node opens the conflict detail panel with envelope data
BAS: Keyboard-only navigation (Tab, Enter, arrow keys) traverses all graph nodes and triggers the same interactions as mouse clicks
BAS: Screen-reader announces node label and conflict status when node receives focus
A developer can identify all conflicted files in a domain without reading the CLI output
Accessible text alternatives allow screen-reader users to obtain the same architecture information as sighted users

title: UI Graph Visualization
